test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 21 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

The mother said to the child, "Don't touch the hot iron."

options.text: The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.
The mother told the child not to touched the hot iron.
The mother warned the child not to be touching the hot iron.
The mother requested the child never to touching the hot iron.

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech in the form of an imperative sentence with a negative command: **"Don't touch the hot iron."**
 
• When converting such sentences into indirect speech, we use the reporting verb **"warned"** to indicate caution.
 
• The word **"not"** is used before the verb to maintain the negative meaning.
 
• The infinitive form of the verb (**"to touch"**) is used in the indirect narration.

Correct sentence: *The mother warned the child not to touch the hot iron.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Option 2:** "The mother told the child not to touched the hot iron." 
 
Grammatically incorrect because "touched" is the past tense, whereas the infinitive "to touch" should have been used.
 
• **Option 3:** "The mother warned the child not to be touching the hot iron." 
 
Incorrect because "not to be touching" is not a suitable structure in indirect speech.
 
• **Option 4:** "The mother requested the child never to touching the hot iron." 
 
Incorrect because "requested" does not convey the warning tone, and "to touching" is grammatically wrong.
 
 
</ul
